title: Study of the atmospheric turbulence measurement by a probe on a light drone
author: Iuri Alexandre Cernov de Oliveira Barbosa
abstract: The utilization of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) for meteorological data acquisition is very profitable if compared to others options: it has a very low cost of operation; it can fly in restricted areas for airplanes; and it can perform several types of missions. For researches related to the atmospheric boundary layer, the utilization of a light drone of meteorological acquisition proves to be very efficient. The Laboratoire d';Aérologie, part of Observatoire Midi-Pyrénées in Toulouse (subordinate to CNRS) invests in the development of an electrical UAV for this purpose, with a maximum takeoff weight of 3 kilograms, having as a first objective the participation on the DACCIWA project, which will take place in Benin, Africa. The graduate work shown here shows the theoretical considerations for turbulence (wind components relative to the ground), temperature and relative humidity of the air calculations; the used equipment, like the airplane and the probes; the realized tests, which includes the calibration of the sensors in a wind tunnel; and the first flight tests realized by the airplane.
